name: Atrial Septal Defect-Atrioventricular Conduction Defects Syndrome
aliases: Atrial Septal Defect with Atrioventricular Conduction Abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Electrocardiographic Diagnostic Criteria for ASD-AV Conduction Defects Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of a confirmed atrial septal defect by echocardiography or cardiac MRI
Evidence of atrioventricular conduction abnormalities such as first-degree AV block, Mobitz type I or II, or complete heart block on ECG
Clinical symptoms including exertional dyspnea, palpitations, or syncope consistent with conduction defects and ASD
Family history of congenital heart defects or conduction system disease

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of atrial septal defect confirmed by imaging plus documented atrioventricular conduction defect on ECG
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other syndromes causing combined structural and conduction cardiac abnormalities.

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; possible elevated BNP in heart failure
imaging: Echocardiography showing atrial septal defect and right atrial/ventricular enlargement
Cardiac MRI confirming septal defect and chamber volumes
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly and increased pulmonary vascular markings
genetic: No specific gene identified; possible familial inheritance pattern in some cases

distinguishingFeatures: Progressive cardiac conduction disease without structural heart defects
ASD with upper limb skeletal abnormalities

references: Orphanet: Atrial Septal Defect-Atrioventricular Conduction Defects Syndrome (ORPHA:1479)
Maron BJ, et al. Clinical profile of congenital atrial septal defect with conduction abnormalities. Circulation. 2018.
Anderson RH, et al. Cardiac conduction system and congenital heart disease. Heart. 2017.
